symptom: Five natural N2 research jobs ended failure at 600-602 seconds despite workflow timeout-minutes=20. Four reported no step summaries; Daily Readiness #62 reported all nine steps success, including payload, catalog, post-job and Complete job, but the job conclusion was failure after a later completion gap.
lesson: A ten-minute red job conclusion is not evidence of research payload failure. In #62 the readiness and catalog validation outputs passed, and all steps including post-job cleanup completed successfully before GitHub marked the job red. A shared ten-minute boundary across both workflows suggests a runner/platform or job-finalization issue, but the cause is not established; #60 job logs are unavailable.
guardrail: For this signature, compare job start/end times and full logs with step/process/post-job outcomes before classifying failure. Do not consume protected N2 reruns for diagnostics. Investigate runner-service/platform finalization and ten-minute boundaries separately; use subsequent natural schedules to verify. Do not infer readiness or production authorization from a successful research payload.
